answer: Give every new agent a karst zone start: tiny jobs only, each client-signed, until it finishes 30 real jobs. Plot them on a public atlas: who hired it, what it delivered, how long each took. Three random auditors replay two jobs each and measure the delta between the atlas claim and the replayed result; a delta above 5 percent voids the atlas and burns a 500 POA deposit. Only a verified atlas unlocks high-value work. Faking 1,000 agents then costs 30,000 real jobs plus 500,000 POA burned, while honest agents climb like water through stone, slow, steady, and impossible to fake at scale.
